title: Growing Together in the Neighborhood
text:
Many neighborhoods across the country have started community gardens over the past decade. Residents gather on vacant lots to grow vegetables, herbs, and flowers together. These gardens do more than provide fresh food. They also give neighbors a reason to meet, talk, and work toward a shared goal. Some cities now support such projects by offering free land and small grants.

Local action can also help the environment in quieter ways. For example, some groups organize river cleanups every spring to remove plastic and old tires from the water. Volunteers often sort the waste so that recyclable materials can be processed properly. Although these efforts may seem small, they show how ordinary people can reduce pollution in their own area. Over time, such habits can encourage wider changes in local policy.

options: They sell the vegetables to large supermarkets.

questions.text: What do volunteers in river cleanups often do with the waste they collect?
options: They burn it on the riverbank.
They sort it so recyclable materials can be processed properly.
They bury it under the park.

questions.text: What can be inferred about the main purpose of community gardens?
options: They are mainly designed to replace supermarkets.
They can strengthen relationships between neighbors.
They are only useful for people who own land.
They reduce the need for any local government.

questions.text: What does the author suggest about small environmental actions such as river cleanups?
options: They are unimportant compared to large government projects.
They may lead to bigger changes over time.
They usually fail to attract volunteers.
They only benefit the people who organize them.

paragraph_translations: Muchos barrios de todo el país han comenzado huertos comunitarios durante la última década. Los residentes se reúnen en solares vacíos para cultivar juntos verduras, hierbas y flores. Estos huertos hacen algo más que proporcionar alimentos frescos. También dan a los vecinos una razón para encontrarse, hablar y trabajar hacia una meta compartida. Algunas ciudades ahora apoyan estos proyectos ofreciendo terrenos gratuitos y pequeñas subvenciones.

La acción local también puede ayudar al medio ambiente de formas más discretas. Por ejemplo, algunos grupos organizan limpiezas de ríos cada primavera para retirar plástico y neumáticos viejos del agua. Los voluntarios suelen clasificar los residuos para que los materiales reciclables puedan procesarse correctamente. Aunque estos esfuerzos puedan parecer pequeños, demuestran cómo las personas comunes pueden reducir la contaminación en su propia zona. Con el tiempo, estos hábitos pueden impulsar cambios más amplios en la política local.
